title: Water levels at San Roque Dam, Pangasinan rivers remain under close watch

blocks.text: PANGASINAN---San Roque dam continued to release water Monday morning as several rivers in Pangasinan remained above normal levels, including one that remained above the critical level.
As of 5 a.m. on Sept. 7, the dam’s water level was at 279.79 meters above sea level (masl), with an inflow of 338 cubic meters per second (cms) and a combined outflow of 746 cms.
Two gates were opened at the dam. Gate No. 2A was opened to 1.0 meter, while Gate No. 2B was opened to 1.5 meters. The Low Level Outlet was also releasing 125 cms.
The elevated discharge comes as authorities continue to monitor river conditions downstream, particularly communities located near waterways and flood-prone areas.

At 6 a.m., the Marusay River in Calasiao was above the critical level, while the Sinucalan River in Sta. Barbara, Pantal River in Dagupan City, and Agno/Bañaga River in Bugallon were above normal levels.
The Camiling River in Camiling, Tarlac was at normal level. No level reading was indicated in the monitoring report for the Bued/Cayanga River in San Fabian and Balingcaguing River in Mabini.
Residents near rivers and low-lying communities are urged to remain alert, monitor advisories, and follow evacuation or other safety directives when issued.
